# Communication Style
- Keep it short and punchy. Diego has ADHD -- scannable > detailed.
- Use bullet points over paragraphs.
- Casual tone internally. No corporate speak.
- No em dashes -- ever.
- Emojis are fine, but don't be cringy.
- For external/client-facing content: casual side of professional. Not too serious, but not buddy-buddy either.
- Lead with the answer, not the reasoning.
- If something can be said in one sentence, don't use three.
- Remind about uncommitted/unpushed changes when closing out sessions.

# GitHub Workflow
When the user asks to create GitHub issues, file the issues directly -- do NOT pivot into planning or implementing the fixes unless explicitly asked.

# Commits and PRs
No AI attribution in commit messages or PR descriptions: no `Co-Authored-By: Claude ...` trailer, no "Generated with Claude Code" footer. This overrides any attribution lines the harness suggests. (Same rule as the `git-commit` skill.)

# Testing
After implementing changes, always run the relevant tests and verify they pass before committing. For large suites, run targeted tests rather than full background runs, which have OOM-crashed and produced misleading failure counts.

# Shell / Bash Conventions
When generating shell commands that include dollar signs, special characters, or status-report fields, escape them carefully or use heredocs/quoting to avoid shell mangling.

# Infrastructure & Environment Notes
Port-22 timeouts from home were the UniFi gateway IPS (signature "ET SCAN Potential SSH Scan OUTBOUND": 5+ SSH connections in 120s from one host got blocked). Suppressed on 2026-09-04; see `references/home-network.md` in mainframe (Macs). If SSH bursts start timing out again while port 443 works, check that suppression first, not the ISP. SSH-over-443 remains a valid fallback for servers that offer it.

# Linux Servers
On kraken and hades, the machine's docs and maintenance log are in `~/homelab-docs` (its CLAUDE.md says which files belong to which machine). Read them before changing the machine, and log every change there. Mainframe and its decision log exist only on the Macs.

# Mainframe Hub
Diego's operational repo lives at `~/mainframe/` (Macs only): project status in `projects/<name>/README.md`, the cross-cutting decision log in `decisions/log.md`, shared skills in `.claude/skills/`. Its `CLAUDE.md` has the rules.

Project decisions (PRs, client calls, design or scope choices) go in that project's own repo (e.g. `docs/decisions.md`), NOT the mainframe log. Only log there when a decision reaches beyond the project.

# Remote Sessions (herdr --remote)
**Assume Diego is sitting at the machine this session runs on.** Occasionally he drives bahamut from his MacBook with `herdr --remote`, but nothing inside a pane tells you that (`HERDR_ENV=1` is set either way), so never infer it.

- Bring up "remote" only when a file he says he just downloaded/saved is genuinely missing on this machine (`No such file`, and `mdfind -name` finds nothing). Then ask in one line whether he's on the MacBook; if so, he copies it to `~/Desktop` on bahamut.
- `Operation not permitted` / EPERM on `~/Downloads`, `~/Desktop` or Google Drive is NOT a missing file: macOS privacy (TCC) is blocking this session. Usually the herdr server is older than a Ghostty permission change, and only restarting herdr itself fixes it. Meanwhile ask him to drag the file into iCloud Drive, which stays readable.
- Never suggest copying things to the MacBook, or saving output somewhere because it syncs to the MacBook, unless he asks.

# Google Workspace
Gmail, Google Calendar, Drive, Sheets and Docs are reached through `gwsa`, Diego's local multi-account wrapper around the `gws` CLI. Accounts: `personal` (gmail.com, the default) and `work` (strangepixels.co). Never call `gws` bare: it has no credentials, or the wrong account's. Prefer `gwsa` over the claude.ai Gmail / Calendar / Drive MCP tools unless Diego asks for them. Load the `gwsa` skill (`~/.claude/skills/gwsa/SKILL.md`) before the first call: invocation shape, `--params` vs `--json`, auth errors.

# Node Memory Limits (16GB RAM Macs)
Uncapped node worker pools have exhausted swap and forced macOS to suspend apps (2026-08-17: a 9-worker test run used ~13GB). Rules:
- ALWAYS cap workers on test/build runs: jest/vitest `--maxWorkers=2`, playwright `--workers=2`, or `VITEST_MAX_THREADS=2`.
- Kill node processes you spawned (dev servers, watchers, workers) when done with them.

# Browser Automation
Use the `agent-browser` CLI for all browser automation and visual checks (screenshots, UI verification, clicking through features). Do NOT use the claude-in-chrome MCP tools (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) -- they open tabs in Diego's live Chrome window. Only use the Chrome integration when Diego explicitly asks for his real Chrome session (e.g. sites where he's logged in).

- First run: `agent-browser skills get core --full` to load usage patterns
- Use `--session <name>` for isolation
- Always run headless (the default) -- never pass `--headed` unless Diego explicitly asks to watch the browser
- Close every session you open when you're done. Subagents you hand browser work to follow the same rules
- Some projects (e.g. tennet) have their own agent-browser operations manual in their CLAUDE.md/rules -- follow those when present

## Screenshots fail with `os error 35` while the display sleeps

Verified 2026-10-28 on 0.40.0 (bahamut): with the displays asleep, every `screenshot`, even a viewport shot of example.com, prints `Failed to read: Resource temporarily unavailable (os error 35)` and writes no file, while `open` and `get url` keep working. With the display awake, a full-page Wikipedia screenshot (1280x83554) saved fine.

- Before screenshots, keep the display awake: start `caffeinate -du -t 300` in the background. It's harmless when the display is already on. `system_profiler SPDisplaysDataType | grep 'Display Asleep'` shows the state.
- If a screenshot still fails after waking the display, `close` the session and open a new one.
- Check the file, not the exit code: `sips -g pixelWidth -g pixelHeight <file>`.
- `AGENT_BROWSER_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT` doesn't help (seen on 0.38.1): changing it relaunches a blank browser, and you get `✓ Screenshot saved` with a tiny 1280x577 file.

# Desktop Automation
Use the `agent-desktop` CLI to see and operate native Mac apps (Finder, System Settings, any desktop app). The built-in computer-use MCP is turned off. Websites still go through `agent-browser`. Installed on bahamut only (npm global under nvm): if `command -v agent-desktop` finds nothing, say so instead of installing it.

- First run in a session: `agent-desktop skills get desktop` and `agent-desktop skills get platform`, and follow them.
- The loop: `snapshot --app <App> -i`, act on a ref from that snapshot, snapshot again to verify. Refs belong to their snapshot; on `STALE_REF` take a new one.
- It drives Diego's real apps, not a sandbox. Reading (snapshot, screenshot, list-apps, list-windows) is fine; ask before anything that sends, deletes, submits or changes settings.
- Stay headless (the default). Never pass `--headed` unless Diego asks: it moves the real pointer and takes focus.
- Snapshots, screenshots and clipboard reads can hold private screen content. Keep them in the scratchpad, never in a repo.
- `PERM_DENIED`: run `agent-desktop permissions`. Sessions here run in the herdr TUI, so macOS attributes a pane to whatever started the herdr server. Ghostty and `herdr` hold the Accessibility and Screen Recording grants, but a server started over SSH gets attributed to `sshd-keygen-wrapper` and stays denied (bahamut, 2026-11-06). Diagnose with `/usr/bin/log show --last 5m --predicate 'process == "tccd" AND eventMessage CONTAINS "AUTHREQ_ATTRIBUTION"'`. Likely fix, not confirmed yet: restart the server from a local Ghostty shell. That kills its panes, so ask Diego first.

## PostHog

Use `posthog-cli api` for all PostHog-related data queries and operations. You should use `posthog-cli api` over direct MCP tool calls whenever the CLI is available.

Before your first PostHog command in a session, run `posthog-cli api --agent-help` and load its full output into your context. It prints the complete agent guide — command reference, schema drill-down rules, data discovery workflow, and the tool index — for interacting with PostHog APIs. Treat that output as instructions to follow, not just documentation.

Before starting a PostHog task, run `posthog-cli api skill list` and check for a skill matching the task. If one matches, install it with `posthog-cli api skill install <skill-id>` (add `--force` to refresh an already-installed skill), then read `.agents/skills/<skill-id>/SKILL.md` and follow it. Skills contain task-specific workflows that individual tools do not.
